figures.caption: Median |B| at t = 3 in a disc of radius 0.06 around the centre of the upper vortex, for each grid. Grey: the 4096² reference averaged to the same cells; dotted: the field that was there at the start. A method on the grey line keeps the region as clean as the reference; one above it has put field there.
figures.differs: Not a figure of the paper: its leakage (Fig. 5) reduced to one number per run, so that all grids and methods fit on one axis.
figures.finding: At 128², the six AthenaK, RAMSES and Athena++ set-ups have 0.9 to 1.8 times the reference's field there; the GLM kernels 11 to 110 times; the CT prototype 389 times. At 512², the six AthenaK, RAMSES and Athena++ set-ups have 1.0 times the reference's field there; the GLM kernels 8 to 13 times; the CT prototype 3.38 times. At t = 1.2, before the vortices have rolled up, the GLM kernels are still within a factor 1.3 of the reference (256²).

figures.title: Kelvin–Helmholtz with a sudden timestep change: field strength and cleaning variable, N = 128
figures.caption: At t = 3 the timestep is cut to 1/40 for 100 steps, then restored. Left: |B| just before the change and at the next two outputs; right: the cleaning variable ψ at the same times. Kernels whose cleaning speed follows 1/Δt (LLF, f16/HLL, HLLD, PPM) are the paper's "v" models; constant c_h is its D1c; CT is its CT.
figures.differs: Our box is the periodic unit square with two shear layers (y = 1/4 and 3/4) instead of one layer with outflow boundaries, so two vortices appear, half a box apart in x; CFL 0.25 instead of 0.4. Our outputs are 0.1 apart, so the paper's snapshots 10⁻⁴ to 4×10⁻² after the change are not available as images; the next figure resolves those steps.

figures.title: Sudden timestep change: the cleaning variable against time, and the field it leaves behind, N = 256
figures.caption: Left: largest |ψ| at every output and, from the timestep change (dashed line) to 300 steps after it, at every step. Middle: the same around the change. Right: median |B| inside the field-free upper vortex just before the change (open marks) and at the end of the run (filled), with their ratio; grey line: the reference at t = 3.
figures.differs: The paper uses a fixed timestep before the change; ours is the CFL step (0.25), cut to 1/40 for 100 steps. "Before" is taken from the run without the change, which is the same solution up to t = 3 (bit for bit at 128², where both states are kept).
figures.finding: With a cleaning speed that follows 1/Δt the largest ψ jumps 15- to 59-fold, and at the end of the run the field inside the field-free vortex is 9.19 to 223 times what it was before the change on 512² (1.95 to 45 times on 256², 1.1 to 27 on 128²). With the constant speed ψ changes by a factor 1.2 to 1.5 and that field by 0.8 to 1.1; in the CT prototype the field changes by 1.1 to 1.2. The paper reports about a 40-fold jump of ψ in its variable-speed models and no effect with a constant speed or CT.

figures.title: Mach 9 decay: spectra of the 256³ runs divided by the 512³ reference
figures.caption: Velocity (left) and magnetic (right) power spectra of each 256³ run divided by the 512³ reference's at the same time, at the first output (t = 0.02, the paper's time) and at the end. Dotted lines: the paper's ±25 % tolerance; the wavenumber where a curve leaves it, as a fraction of the Nyquist wavenumber, is the effective bandwidth (table below). At t = 0.02 our smooth start has only just formed its first shocks, so t = 0.2 is the fairer time to read.
figures.differs: Every code starts from the same smooth random velocity field at rms Mach 9 with a uniform field (β₀ = 22), not from the paper's driven, saturated state, so the field is first amplified here; values are not comparable with the paper's, the kind of measurement is. γ = 1.01 instead of isothermal. The paper's reference is its least diffusive code at 1024³ filtered to 256³; ours is AthenaK PLM/HLLE at 512³, unfiltered, which is itself a second-order scheme.

figures.finding: At 512³ the magnetic-to-kinetic energy ratio grows 258 to 351-fold by the end of the run and ends at 0.29 to 0.39 over the 5 set-ups that finish (largest over smallest: 1.36); by code: GLM 0.29, CT prototype 0.30, AthenaK and Athena++ 0.34, RAMSES 0.39; the divergence measure of the GLM kernels ends at 0.013, the CT prototype's face divergence at 3.2×10⁻⁶. The paper's Fig. 5 has, for the disc, about 10⁻¹⁶ for RAMSES (CT), 10⁻² for ART (Dedner) and 10⁻¹ for AREPO and SWIFT, and the two grid codes several orders of magnitude below equipartition where AREPO and SWIFT reach 10–20 %.
figures.title: Field amplification in the Mach 9 decay at 512³: energy ratio, divergence error and kinetic energy against time
figures.caption: Left: volume-averaged magnetic over kinetic energy. Centre: a dimensionless divergence error, for the codes that carry one: the GLM kernels (centred differences of their cell-centred field) and the CT prototype (the face-centred divergence it preserves, at single-precision rounding). AthenaK, RAMSES and Athena++ keep their face-centred divergence at rounding by construction; it is not in the saved cell-centred states and is not drawn. Right: kinetic energy.
figures.differs: The paper's Fig. 5 is for the gas disc of an isolated galaxy (radius 15 kpc, height 0.5 kpc) over 7 Gyr, with self-gravity, cooling and a pressure floor, where shear winds up a 10⁻¹² G seed field; ours is a periodic box of decaying Mach 9 turbulence with a uniform field (β₀ = 22) over 0.2 box sound-crossing times, with no gravity or cooling. The paper compares grid, moving-mesh and particle codes; all of ours are fixed grids, so this shows only the spread among grid codes and where a GLM code falls in it. Their divergence error is the volume mean of |∇·B|Δx/|B| in the disc; ours is rms(∇·B)Δx over rms(B) in the whole box.

figures.title: AREPO, static against moving mesh: the field loop, the timestep, and the divergence of B
figures.finding: On the static mesh the magnetic energy of the advected field loop grows instead of decaying: by a factor of 3.49 at 32², 5.3×10³ at 64², 2.6×10⁵ at 128², 2.3×10⁵ at 256², 9.0×10³ at 512² at its largest; on the moving mesh at 256² it ends at 0.9994 of its initial value; AREPO ended 7 static-mesh runs itself when its timestep fell to the smallest its time line holds (current sheet 256² at t = 1.92; field loop 256² at t = 0.839; field loop 512² at t = 0.556; field loop novz 256² at t = 0.883; field loop novz 512² at t = 0.398; orszag tang 256² at t = 0.422; orszag tang 512² at t = 0.293); AREPO's own divergence measure at the end of the four tests shown is 0.013 to 0.064 on the moving mesh at every grid and 1.8×10⁻³ to 0.028 on the static mesh.
figures.caption: (a) Magnetic energy of the field loop advected in the plane, over its initial value, on AREPO's static Cartesian mesh at four grids and on its moving mesh; a cross is where AREPO ended the run. (b) The timestep of the static-mesh runs AREPO ended, over its first value, against the part of the run done (from AREPO's own log). (c) AREPO's own measure of the divergence of B at the last output, rms(∇·B) × cell size over rms(B) on its own mesh, against the grid.
figures.differs: AREPO was run with Powell's eight-wave scheme, the HLLD solver, one global timestep and Courant factor 0.3, on the suite's periodic unit box. A static mesh with Powell's scheme is not how AREPO is normally run; its published MHD results use the moving mesh. Two checks of Orszag–Tang at 256² on the static mesh: on one rank it stops at the same step, and with half the Courant factor it stops slightly later (t = 0.454 against 0.422).

figures.title: Convergence on the wave tests, with AREPO among the other codes
figures.finding: Errors at the end of the run: entropy wave, moving mesh: 8.5×10⁻⁷ at 32² to 1.9×10⁻⁷ at 512² (order 0.5); entropy wave, static mesh: 3.8×10⁻³ at 32² to 1.8×10⁻⁵ at 512² (order 1.9); oblique Alfvén wave, moving mesh: 9.2×10⁻³ at 32² to 4.8×10⁻⁵ at 512² (order 1.9); oblique Alfvén wave, static mesh: 7.0×10⁻³ at 32² to 3.9×10⁻⁵ at 512² (order 1.9). On the moving mesh the entropy wave is carried by the mesh itself, so its error is at the precision of the saved single-precision states at every grid.
figures.caption: Error at the end of the run against the grid for the entropy wave and the two Alfvén waves. Top: the GLM kernels and the CT prototype. Bottom: AthenaK, RAMSES, Athena++ and AREPO (ochre; solid the moving mesh, dashed the static mesh).
